note: A place-by-place sweep of FamilySearch's indexed Croatian and Istrian records for this surname and its variants, run in September 2026 across sixty towns and parishes from Muggia to Senj. What follows is where the name is indexed, where it is not, and — importantly — why a blank is not an absence.
lead: The archive had searched by name. This searches by place, one parish at a time, which is the only way to see the shape of a surname across a province. Sixty places; twenty-one return the name; thirty-nine return nothing. Two of the twenty-one push the surname back further in Istria than anything else this project has found.
method: For each place, the top hundred indexed persons matching Defranceschi were pulled and kept only if the record's own place text actually names that town and the name is a Franceschi form. Counts are of matched index entries, not of distinct people — a single baptism can appear more than once — so read them as weight, not as population.

clusters.who: Antonio, Mattio, Pietro, Maria, Virginia Lambertina Defranceschi
clusters.note: The heaviest concentration anywhere in the sweep, and it starts in 1742 — two years after the Giovanni Battista whom Kobler traced arriving from the County of Pazin «intorno al 1740». Carlo's own account of the Fiume branch lands exactly here.

clusters.who: Natale Mattio, Angelo, Vitorio, Elisabetta, Irene De Franceschi
clusters.note: Carlo's book names Franceschi among the noble families of Pola «venuti da Capodistria» before the plague of 1631, and a Sabba de Franceschi of Bologna licensed in 1562 to settle families there. This is a third and much larger presence, a century and a half later.
With Premantura and Medulin this makes a real southern-Istrian group around the tip of the peninsula, entirely separate from the central-Istrian line.
All the Senj hits are Franceschini or Franceskini, not Defranceschi — a different formation of the same root, and a caution against treating the two as one family.

clusters.who: Mattio, Domenico Gasparo, Zuana, Marina, Maria Maddalena De Franceschi
clusters.note: The oldest cluster in Istria, and the most interesting single result of the sweep. A settled De Franceschi household at Svetvinčenat in the 1670s, bearing the name Zuana — the Venetian form of Giovanni, the same form as the Zuane of the 1679 Mione list. It is contemporaneous with everything the Carnia argument turns on, and nobody in this project had looked at Svetvinčenat.

clusters.who: Carlo Franceschi, Amelia and Mario Franceschini, Iolanda Franceschi
Giorgius, Nicolò, Giorgio, Margarita Maria, Nadalina Defranceschi
clusters.note: Promontore, at the very southern tip.

clusters.who: Joannem, Maria Anna, Antoniam, Nodburgam Defranceschi, Francisca Paula Franceskini
clusters.note: Including a Nodburga — a rare Germanic saint's name, and one the family already holds a record image of.

clusters.who: Franciscus, Joannes Aloysius, Josephus, Maria Defranceschi

clusters.note: Carlo was appointed to the court at Rovinj in 1850 and his son Camillo took refuge there in the war.

The single earliest indexed occurrence of the surname anywhere in Istria: 1615, at Albona. Sixty-four years before the Mione headmen's list, and eighty-five before the date Carlo gives for his family's arrival.

clusters.who: Conraddus Vincentius and Liberatus Francus Xaverius Defranceschi
clusters.note: Two elaborate Latin names in one year. Vincenzo is one of the names Carlo says the Zadar branch keeps, and a Vincenzo was Chancellor of the County of Pazin in that century.
A compound Slavicised form. The map the family keeps traces Barban emigrants to Moselle, Cannes and Charleville in France.

clusters.who: Anna Maria Defranceschi, José de Franceschi

clusters.note: One entry, and it carries the exact name-form of Carlo's great-great-grandfather.

caveat.heading: Why the blanks prove nothing at all
caveat.text: Gračišće returns nothing. Gologorica returns nothing. Crikvenica returns nothing. This archive has, in its own files, the 1863 baptism at Gračišće, the Status Animarum of Gallignana, the 1890 baptism at Klenovica and four Crikvenica register entries — all of them for this family, none of them findable by this search. The reason is simple: those registers are on FamilySearch as browse-only images that no volunteer has indexed. A blank in the table above means «not typed up», not «not there». It is the single most important thing to understand about searching this surname, and it is why the real work of this project has been done in scans and archives rather than in search boxes.
caveat.then: Read the other way, the blanks are a work list. Every parish above with a nil return and a known register is a place where a morning of page-turning could produce something no search will ever surface.

reading.h: There is no single Istrian family of this name
reading.t: The sweep shows at least four groups that do not obviously touch: a Rijeka–Bakar concentration from 1742; a Pula–Ližnjan–Premantura–Medulin group in the far south from about 1778; a scatter across the north-west at Kaštelir, Oprtalj, Roč, Šterna and Vrsar; and the central-Istrian line at Gračišće and Gologorica that this archive follows, which the index cannot see at all. Add Labin in 1615 and Svetvinčenat in the 1670s and the picture is of a patronymic surname arising and arriving repeatedly, not of one trunk.

reading.h: But two results are worth chasing hard
reading.t: Svetvinčenat 1674–1710 and Labin 1615 are both older than the Mione list of 1679, and both older than the 1700 date Carlo gives for his family reaching Istria. If the De Franceschi were already at Albona in 1615, the tidy story of a single Carnian arrival around 1700 is at best incomplete.

Šterna, 1807, «Gio Batta De Franceschi». Carlo's great-great-grandfather was Giambattista del fu Leonardo, who built the Gologorica house in 1711. This is a different man in a different century, but the name-form runs in a family and Šterna is two hours' walk from Oprtalj, where the Franceschini are.

next: Svetvinčenat parish registers, 1650–1720 — the oldest cluster and the least examined. Ask whether the Mattio and Zuana of the 1670s have parents in the book.
Labin (Albona) 1600–1650, for the Aloysius Defranceschi of 1615.
Rijeka 1740–1760, for the Giovanni Battista who came from the County of Pazin — Carlo's own great-uncle's line.
Ližnjan, Premantura and Medulin as one southern group: are they one family across three parishes?
And the thirty-nine blanks, one register at a time.
